name: Sterling-Nakamura Emergency Transponder ET-5
description: A concealed emergency beacon that, when activated, broadcasts an encrypted distress signal containing the user's identity, location, biometric status, and a 10-second audio recording to Sterling-Nakamura's security response network. The ET-5 is designed to be activated covertly — a specific gesture, a pressure pattern, or a neural interface command — without alerting nearby threats. The beacon transmits through multiple redundant channels including satellite, cellular, and mesh network, ensuring the signal gets out even in jammed environments. Sterling-Nakamura guarantees a response within 15 minutes in covered areas.

specifications.info: pressure pattern; or neural command; pendant; or subdermal implant

story_hooks: An ET-5 activated inside a sealed underground chamber where no signal should have escaped — the beacon's mesh network redundancy found a path through building wiring, and the response team arrived within 20 minutes.
An ET-5 signal was received from a user who was confirmed dead 6 hours prior — either the beacon malfunctioned, or someone is wearing a dead person's emergency transponder.
